tagline: A fundraising workspace: an investor CRM with AI profile extraction, a TSX graphics studio, and pitch decks you build slide by slide with an AI coach.
summary: My Fundraise keeps a founder's raise in one place. **Investors** holds firms and their contacts; paste a firm's website text or a contact sheet and Claude extracts the profile and people for you. **Pitch decks** are ordered slides, each with a studio where an AI coach — grounded in your **business context** (sections and facts about the company) — helps you write and tighten the slide, and you can track which investors each deck was sent to.

Slides and other visuals are authored as TSX in the **graphics studio** with live preview and PNG export, optionally drafted by a Cursor agent. A seeded demo deck ("Deck E") shows the full flow, including a live review page. Data now lives in local Postgres behind a storage server; the API reaches it directly or through the studio gateway.
audience: Founders running a seed or pre-seed raise who track investors in spreadsheets today.
You want help writing deck slides that stay consistent with the facts about your company.
You're comfortable designing slides as React/Tailwind TSX.
notFor: Investor discovery databases — you bring the investors; it organizes and enriches them.
Sending emails or tracking opens — deck sends are logged manually.
Teams — no sign-in; a single dev user id is used for AI ledgers.

capabilities.title: Investors CRM
capabilities.detail: `/investors` and `/investor-detail-page`: firms, contacts and deck sends.

capabilities.title: AI investor extraction
capabilities.detail: Extract a firm profile or a contact sheet from pasted text via Claude (`/api/investor-extract/*`), each with its own request/response/exchange ledger.

capabilities.title: Business context
capabilities.detail: `/business-context-page` stores sections and facts about your company that ground every AI answer.

capabilities.title: Pitch decks
capabilities.detail: `/pitch-decks` and `/pitch-deck-detail-page`: ordered slides (reorder, versions), intro-slide graphics and send log.

capabilities.title: Slide studio coach
capabilities.detail: Per-slide AI guidance with a ledger per deck and slide (`/api/pitch-deck-slide-studio/*`).

capabilities.title: Graphics studio
capabilities.detail: `/graphics` and `/graphics-studio`: TSX editor with in-browser compile, live preview and PNG export; optional Cursor-agent TSX generation.

capabilities.title: Deck E live review
capabilities.detail: `/deck-e-live-review-page` walks through the seeded demo deck.

components.name: Web app
components.owns: Landing, investors, decks, slide studio, graphics studio, business context, API docs. Calls the API at `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL`.

components.name: API
components.owns: `/api/data/*` entity routes, investor extract, slide studio, business context, Cursor TSX generation, API docs catalog.
components.doesNotOwn: SQL — it invokes the storage server (direct or gateway).

components.name: Storage server
components.owns: `my_fundraise` Postgres: investors, contacts, decks, slides, sends, graphics, business context, AI ledgers, `dispatcher_exposed_endpoints`.

dataFlow: The web app calls the API (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL`) and sends `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_USER_ID` for AI features.
The API invokes storage: **direct** (`MY_FUNDRAISE_STORAGE_URL` + secret) or **gateway** (`CANONICAL_DATA_ACCESS_MODE=gateway`, `MY_FUNDRAISE_GATEWAY_*`).
Investor extraction and slide coaching send your text plus business context to Anthropic and store each exchange.
Graphics TSX is compiled and previewed in the browser; Cursor generation (if configured) writes TSX via `CURSOR_TARGET_REPO`.

trust.title: Browser
trust.detail: API URL and a dev user id only. TSX you paste runs in the browser preview — treat it as trusted.

trust.title: API
trust.detail: Holds `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CURSOR_API_KEY` and the storage/gateway secret. No user auth.

trust.title: Anthropic / Cursor
trust.detail: Receive investor text, business facts and slide content when you use AI.

commonTasks.title: First-time setup
steps: Run **Setup** in Hub (add the storage repo path to hub.local.json first — see Hub notes).
On the **Storage Express** repo, **Set up local database** to create `my_fundraise` and apply `migrations/` (`010_seed_deck_e_on_prem_graphics.sql` is optional demo data).
On the API set `MY_FUNDRAISE_STORAGE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3097`, `MY_FUNDRAISE_STORAGE_SECRET` (= storage `STORAGE_DISPATCHER_SECRET`) and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
On the web set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL` to the API's port and `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_USER_ID`.

commonTasks.title: Add an investor from their website
commonTasks.when: You found a firm to pitch.
steps: Create the investor on `/investors` and open it.
Paste the firm's profile text and run extract; paste a team page or contact sheet to extract contacts.

commonTasks.title: Build a deck
steps: Fill in `/business-context-page` with your company's facts.
Create a deck on `/pitch-decks`, add and order slides.
Use the slide studio coach on each slide; design visuals in `/graphics-studio` and export PNGs.
Log each send on the investor or deck.

troubleshooting.fix: Storage unreachable or secret mismatch: `curl http://127.0.0.1:3097/api/storage/health` and compare secrets.
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` missing, or `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_USER_ID` not set on the web.
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL` defaults to port 3009; Hub may run the API on 3030.
Set `CURSOR_API_KEY` and `CURSOR_TARGET_REPO`, with the Cursor GitHub App installed on that repo.

glossary.definition: Sections and facts about your company used to ground AI output.
Per-slide AI coach with its own ledger.
A record that a deck went to an investor.
The seeded demo pitch deck and graphics.

hubNotes: hub.local.json has no `storageExpressDir`, though `my-fundraise-storage-express-server` is cloned at `~/github/my-fundraise/`. That folder isn't a git repo yet, and its `.cursor/architecture` includes finance ADRs copied from finances-manager.
The storage cutover isn't committed: the API has ~146 and the web ~76 uncommitted changes; the READMEs still describe Supabase (`docs/sql/001…011`).
The API's `.env.example` uses port 3009 (clashes with several other projects); the registry says 3030.
